openImplementationDecisions.summary: When must settlement finality arrive relative to quote expiry, and how are late-but-settled payments handled (held vs refunded)? Quote expiry is hard-enforced before settlement confirmation in this prototype; delayed settlement lands in EXPIRED_QUOTE with the payment queued for refund (spec §6.3 same-key auto-refund) — the held-vs-refunded choice itself is OPEN.
openImplementationDecisions.prototypeChoiceLabeled: PROTOTYPE CHOICE (LABELED, NOT APPROVED): expiry checked at settlement confirmation; delayed payment → HELD_IN_REFUND_QUEUE (refund state machine per spec §6.3)

openImplementationDecisions.summary: What are the semantics of a payment reversal that arrives after issuance (re-mint? claw-back? burn? operator adjudication?) — none are defined; the prototype fail-closes: RECONCILIATION exception + pipeline SUSPENDED, mint record preserved, NO silent re-mint, NO silent write-off.
openImplementationDecisions.prototypeChoiceLabeled: PROTOTYPE CHOICE (LABELED, NOT APPROVED): fail-closed suspension + exception queue; adjudication left OPEN

openImplementationDecisions.summary: How are failed/expired/unauthorized payments recovered (auto-refund timing, retry policy, compensation authority)? The prototype queues refunds deterministically and forbids retry on the same idempotency key; the real recovery process is OPEN.
openImplementationDecisions.prototypeChoiceLabeled: PROTOTYPE CHOICE (LABELED, NOT APPROVED): PENDING_REFUND → REFUNDED same-key refund queue; retry on same key forbidden

openImplementationDecisions.summary: Where are the atomic transaction boundaries when payment settlement and token issuance live in different systems (spec §14.4 hard rules: safe state machine + idempotency + exception handling + compensating process are mandatory)? The prototype performs each step as a single in-memory commit (L6 analog); real cross-system boundaries are OPEN.
openImplementationDecisions.prototypeChoiceLabeled: PROTOTYPE CHOICE (LABELED, NOT APPROVED): per-step single-commit records; no cross-system atomicity is claimed
